correctness.rationale: Proposition 2, Eq. (6) uses Aθ=1+(3−2q)θ; Theorem 1, Eq. (9) instead defines A=4−2q and specifies the real lower branch. With b=(2−q)θ, z=−bx and q′=1/(2−q), the true inverse satisfies (z−Aθ)exp_q′(z)=−Aθ(1−u). Setting κ=1+(1−q′)A, substitution w=(z−A)/κ verifies that the printed expression solves this equation with A=4−2q rather than Aθ: the two positive bases factor as 1+(1−q′)z=κ[1+(1−q′)w]. When κ>0 and A>1, z<0 implies w<−A/κ<−1/(2−q′), the decreasing (lower) branch, whose endpoint value at z=0 corresponds to u=0 and whose other endpoint to u=1. The printed κ is positive throughout the admissible q intervals. Subtraction gives the stated exact residual, strictly signed as θ−1 for 0<u<1. As an exact check, for (θ,q)=(2,4/3) the printed inverse at u=3/8 gives x=3/2 but the true CDF there is 9/20. With the corrected Aθ, κ=(3−2q)[1−(q−1)θ]/(2−q); the shift divides by zero at κ=0 and loses its positive base at κ<0. Neither prevents monotone numerical CDF inversion: for s=1+(q−1)θx and p=(2−q)/(q−1)>1 on the unbounded side, the survival derivative in s has the sign of (1−p)s−(Aθ−p)<0 for s≥1, regardless of κ. On the bounded side, s=1−(1−q)θx decreases from 1 to 0, and s^p[1+(p/Aθ)(1−s)] for p=(2−q)/(1−q)>1 is strictly increasing in s on (0,1). The four reported medians were independently reproduced by bisection (python /workspace/checks/independent_formula_checks.py); supplied checker inspected without execution. No inference is made about private simulation code.

value.rationale: This identifies the law that the published sampler actually generates if implemented literally, rather than just correcting notation. All four simulation designs are affected; for example the nominal median in the fourth design has actual coverage approximately 0.379.
